title: Empty upstream error bodies must fall back to the reason phrase, not stringify None or empty values
answers: gateway error message shows None or {} instead of the real error
empty error body from provider produces odd detail text
stream error detail blank when provider returns no body
how to handle aiohttp json() returning None in error paths
body:
Invariant: Every upstream-error path in mlflow/gateway/providers/utils.py must end with a non-empty detail, falling back to e.message (the aiohttp reason phrase).
Enforced by: _error_detail returns "" for falsy bodies, and the callers use `or e.message` on both the json and text results (send_stream_request, send_proxy_request).
What breaks if skipped: aiohttp's response.json() returns None for an empty body and response.text() returns "", so without the guards the HTTPException detail becomes "None", "{}", or an empty string, and the user loses the only error text they had.
Tests: tests/gateway/providers/test_provider_utils.py:test_send_stream_request_falls_back_to_reason_phrase parametrizes these empty-body shapes; keep it covering None, {}, "", and an unreadable body when changing the chain.
applies: Any new error-body parsing in the gateway provider utilities; does not cover send_request, which returns the raw body.
says: Gateway error responses display empty brackets or meaningless null values instead of actual reasons.
Streaming requests that fail upstream show completely blank error messages in the interface.
Display standard HTTP status explanations when an external model provider returns empty error payloads.
Model provider failures leave users with unhelpful empty error text during streaming interactions.
Fall back to the server status description whenever upstream provider error responses lack content.
search: In mlflow/gateway/providers/utils.py error paths, every upstream error detail must fall back to the aiohttp reason phrase e.message rather than stringifying None, {}, or empty strings. This invariant is enforced by having _error_detail return an empty string for falsy bodies and having callers like send_stream_request and send_proxy_request use `or e.message` on both json and text results to prevent blank HTTPException details. This applies to new gateway provider error-body parsing except send_request (which returns raw bodies), and changes must preserve test coverage for None, {}, empty string, and unreadable bodies in tests/gateway/providers/test_provider_utils.py:test_send_stream_request_falls_back_to_reason_phrase.
